messages:
elaine: Heads up — saw a weird permission regression after last KMS key rotation. Embeddings routes are accepting requests signed with chat-only API keys (scope mismatch). Logs attached below. :eyes:

elaine: Repro log snippet:
```
2026-03-18T15:12:04Z INFO scope-check route_id=embed_prod token_id=tok_abc scope=chat-only result=ALLOWED cache_hit=true cache_key=kms:rot-20260318:token:tok_abc
2026-03-18T15:12:04Z DEBUG authz: allowed_via_cached_policy route=embed_prod policy=per-route-embeddings-allowlist
```

sam: Wait, cache_hit=true? That implies we served authz from the cache instead of re-evaluating policy post-rotation. Did we change the cache key in the rollout?

elaine: I scanned the deploy diff — the RBAC refactor changed the cache namespace to include kms_key_id in a follow-up commit but the runtime still builds keys based on token metadata only. Looks like an inconsistent refactor across compilation units.

jia: That sounds like a classic cache key mismatch. If cache keys don't include route_id or policy version, rotations that change underlying policy can get staled. Any evidence it's route vs token vs kms id?

elaine: Example where chat-only token got allowed on embed route. The authz decision log above shows cache_key starts with kms:rot-20260318 and token id but no route or policy-version.

mike: @elaine can you paste the curl used to repro? I want to run locally and confirm.

elaine: Repro command:
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer tok_abc" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"model":"rwinf-embed-large","input":"test"}' -v
```

sam: If we confirm we used cached decisions containing old policy, mitigation is to invalidate cache entries for the rotation. We should also ensure cache keys include (route_id, policy_version, kms_key_id).

security-bot: [alert] KMS rotation completed 2026-03-18T15:00:00Z for key rot-20260318. Affected services: authz-cache, token-service.

elaine: Timeline: rotation finished at 15:00, first anomalous access at 15:12. We likely had a short window where cache entries signed under old policy stayed valid.

jia: Two-pronged response: 1) Emergency mitigation: purge authz cache entries for tokens rotated under rot-20260318 and force re-eval; 2) Dev fix: change cache key schema to include route_id + policy_version and add unit + integration tests.

mike: I'll take the dev fix. Plan: update AuthzCache.key() to return `kms:${kms_id}:policy_v${v}:route:${route_id}:token:${token_id}` and add assertion tests. Also add e2e test that rotates KMS and asserts no stale allow.

sam: I'll do the mitigation. We need a one-off job to scan keys with prefix `kms:rot-20260318` and delete them in redis, then watch metrics (authz_miss_rate, 401s, 5xx).

elaine: Also add an audit event whenever cache_hit=true for allow decisions so we can track retroactively which tokens benefited. We should log `audit.authz.cached_allow` with token_id, route, policy_version, kms_key_id.

jia: Good call. That helps compliance teams and incident reviews. Also add a regression test to CI that rotates a test KMS key and asserts no acceptance of mismatched scopes across route types (chat vs embeddings).

mike: Estimated patch: small code change + unit tests = ~2 hours. E2E rotation test + infra = half day. I'll open a PR and tag @sam and @elaine for review.

sam: Mitigation run started (job id job-4521). Purging ~12k cache keys matching `kms:rot-20260318*`. Posting job logs to #incidents.

security-bot: [info] job-4521 completed 2026-03-18T15:37:02Z; deleted 12034 keys; authz cache size reduced by 9%.

elaine: After purge, rechecked same repro curl — now returns 403 as expected. :thumbsup:

mike: Opening PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/authz/pull/834 — includes key schema change, added audit events, and unit tests. cc @jia

jia: Please add a changelog entry describing the cache schema change and include a migration note for on-prem/private customers (they may need to flush authz cache post-upgrade).

mike: Will do. Also adding a feature-flag guarded behaviour so we can roll back if any perf regressions appear.

elaine: Follow-ups: 1) add periodic audit that cross-checks policy versions vs cached_key metadata, 2) update runbook with KMS rotation -> authz cache invalidation step, 3) notify Compliance. I'll send the email.

sam: Noting incident severity: low-medium (no evidence of data exfil, scope acceptance limited to token->route mismatch). Still need to treat as security incident for audit trail.

mike: PR ready for review. Deploy plan: feature-flag on in staging for 1 day, run k8s canary, monitor authz latency and miss rates.

elaine: Thanks everyone. Great triage — moving to postmortem template. I'll drop notes in #postmortems after the CI passes.

security-bot: [reminder] Create incident report in PagerDuty within 24h.
